head.headline: Hearthbook, or the _diary on the front desk?_
head.lede: The eight questions clinics ask us before they switch. Every answer has a source and a date. **Where something else does it better, we say so.**

groups.question: What will it cost over a year?
groups.assumes: One clinic, three practitioners, about 120 bookings a week.

sheet.note: No extra cost on the plan you have

cc.note: Online booking is an add-on module

hb.note: Text the day before, reply to move

diary.note: Reminder calls when there is time

groups.assumes: From signing up to the first patient booking themselves in.

sheet.note: Make the columns, share the link

groups.question: What happens to my data if I leave?
groups.assumes: Patient names, bookings and the notes attached to them.

hb.note: CSV for bookings, PDF for notes

picks.hb: You take 60 or more bookings a week, lose hours to call-backs, and want it working this week.
picks.diary: You see fewer than 30 patients a week and one person answers the phone. It costs almost nothing and never goes offline.
picks.sheet: Lowest cost matters most and call-backs do not bother you. Kept tidy, it carries a clinic to about 60 bookings a week.
picks.cc: You need billing, insurance claims and five or more practitioners in one system, and can give it six weeks.

method: How we compared: a clinic with three practitioners and about 120 bookings a week. Facts about Clinicore come from its public pages on the date shown. Our study figures come from clinics that use each method, measured the same way.
